Align CIF matrices on a common time grid

Source: R/helpers_cif.R
align_cifs.Rd

Aligns a list of cumulative incidence function (CIF) matrices to a common time grid using stepwise constant interpolation. Optionally, the aligned matrices can be concatenated by rows.

Usage

align_cifs(
  x,
  times,
  eval_times = sort(unique(unlist(times, use.names = FALSE))),
  bind_rows = FALSE,
  add_times = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

(list())
List of CIF matrices, with observations in rows and time points in columns. Matrices may have different time grids and numbers of rows.

times

(list())
List of numeric time vectors, matched to the matrices in x by position. Each vector must have one entry per corresponding CIF matrix column.

eval_times

(numeric())
Non-negative, strictly increasing time points at which to evaluate all CIFs. Defaults to the sorted union of the time grids in times.

bind_rows

(logical(1))
If FALSE (default), return a list of aligned matrices. If TRUE, return one matrix by concatenating the aligned matrices by rows.

add_times

(logical(1))
If TRUE, set the output matrices' column names to eval_times. If FALSE (default), no time column names are added.

Value

By default, a list of time-aligned matrices in the same order as x. If bind_rows = TRUE, a single matrix containing all input rows on the common time grid. Each output matrix has one column per evaluation time point.

Details

The input matrices and their time grids are assumed to be valid and already validated with assert_cif_list(). Interpolation uses survdistr::interp_cif() with check = FALSE.

See also

assert_cif_list(), survdistr::interp_cif()

Examples

cif = list(
  Death = matrix(c(0, 0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5), nrow = 2L),
  Relapse = matrix(c(0, 0, 0.1, 0.2), nrow = 2L)
)
times = list(Death = c(0, 2, 4), Relapse = c(1, 3))

# Keep one matrix per cause on the union of the time grids
align_cifs(cif, times, add_times = TRUE)
#> $Death
#>      0 1   2   3   4
#> [1,] 0 0 0.2 0.2 0.4
#> [2,] 0 0 0.3 0.3 0.5
#> 
#> $Relapse
#>      0 1 2   3   4
#> [1,] 0 0 0 0.1 0.1
#> [2,] 0 0 0 0.2 0.2
#> 

# Combine rows on the union of the time grids
align_cifs(cif, times, bind_rows = TRUE, add_times = TRUE)
#>      0 1   2   3   4
#> [1,] 0 0 0.2 0.2 0.4
#> [2,] 0 0 0.3 0.3 0.5
#> [3,] 0 0 0.0 0.1 0.1
#> [4,] 0 0 0.0 0.2 0.2

# Combine rows on an explicit evaluation grid
align_cifs(cif, times, eval_times = c(1.5, 2, 3.5), bind_rows = TRUE, add_times = TRUE)
#>      1.5   2 3.5
#> [1,]   0 0.2 0.2
#> [2,]   0 0.3 0.3
#> [3,]   0 0.0 0.1
#> [4,]   0 0.0 0.2
